from: chapitres 3 et 4 de la vidéo longue (la cotation Urner Barry, la plateforme ECI, la plainte du DOJ et l'accord ; coupé : grippe aviaire, Cal-Maine, rayon)
paragraphs: Most eggs in America aren't priced at the store. They're priced off a daily number from a private company called Urner Barry.
That number is fed by a small trading platform, where egg producers buy and sell spare eggs.
In June {twenty twenty-six|2026}, the Justice Department and {seventeen|17} states said three big egg companies coordinated their bids there, to push that number up.
One email, according to New York's attorney general: strong bids, early and often.
The companies denied it, and settled for {three point three million dollars|$3.3 million} and {fifty-three million|53 million} eggs, with no admission of wrongdoing. Full story on the channel.
